System Design #01: Vertical vs Horizontal Scaling

Two ways to handle more load and when to use each.

• Vertical: simple, but capped and fragile
• Horizontal: near-limitless and fault tolerant
• Horizontal needs stateless services
• Start vertical, scale out when you must

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #02: Latency vs Throughput

The two numbers that define “fast”.

• Latency = time for one request
• Throughput = requests per second
• They often trade off: batching & queues
• Watch p99, not just the average

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #03: Availability & the Nines

How “always up” is actually measured.

• Each nine = 10× less downtime
• SLI measures, SLO targets, SLA promises
• Serial dependencies multiply failure
• Redundancy in parallel adds nines

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #04: CAP Theorem

Why distributed databases must make a choice.

• Partitions will happen: P is mandatory
• CP: errors rather than stale data
• AP: stale data rather than errors
• No partition? See PACELC (next)

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #05: PACELC Theorem

CAP’s missing half: the everyday trade-off.

• PAC = CAP during a partition
• ELC = the everyday trade-off
• Strong consistency always costs latency
• Choose per use case, even per query

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #06: Consistency Models

What a read is allowed to return.

• Consistency is a spectrum, not on/off
• Stronger = slower and less available
• Eventual is fine for most counters & feeds
• Users notice missing read-your-writes first

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #07: Back-of-the-Envelope Estimation

Size a system in 2 minutes, without a calculator.

• 1 day ≈ 10⁵ seconds
• Estimate QPS → storage → bandwidth → servers
• Be roughly right, fast
• Find the bottleneck: that’s the point

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #08: Stateless vs Stateful Services

The secret to scaling out painlessly.

• Stateless servers scale horizontally with ease
• Push state to DBs, caches or tokens
• Sticky sessions are a band-aid
• Keep stateful parts few and well-replicated

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #09: Monolith vs Microservices

One big app, or many small ones?.

• Monolith: simple, fast, one deploy
• Microservices: independent scaling & teams
• You pay in network & operational complexity
• Split when the pain is real, not before

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #10: Single Points of Failure

Find the one thing that can take you down.

• Walk every request path: what if this dies?
• Redundancy + automatic failover
• Check people, certs & vendors too
• Prove it with failure testing

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #11: Client-Server vs Peer-to-Peer

Who does the work: one center, or everyone?.

• Client-server: simple, controllable, central
• P2P: scales with users, no center
• P2P pays in NAT, discovery & trust
• Real systems often mix both

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #12: Functional vs Non-Functional Requirements

What to ask before you draw a single box.

• Functional = features (what)
• Non-functional = qualities (how well)
• Put numbers on every quality
• Agree on what’s out of scope

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #13: How DNS Works

Turning names into IP addresses in milliseconds.

• Resolver → root → TLD → authoritative
• Caching makes most lookups instant
• TTL decides how fast changes spread
• DNS can route, balance and fail over

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #14: TCP vs UDP

Reliable delivery, or raw speed?.

• TCP: reliable, ordered, connection-based
• UDP: fast, simple, no guarantees
• TCP’s reliability costs latency
• Real-time apps often pick UDP (or QUIC)

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #15: HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2 vs HTTP/3

How the web’s protocol keeps getting faster.

• 1.1: one request per connection at a time
• 2: multiplexing over a single TCP connection
• 3: QUIC over UDP, no TCP head-of-line blocking
• Enable HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 at your CDN or proxy

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #16: REST vs GraphQL vs gRPC

Three ways for software to talk.

• REST: simple, cacheable, universal
• GraphQL: flexible queries, fewer round trips
• gRPC: fast, typed, streaming
• Mix them: each layer has a best fit

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #17: WebSockets, SSE & Long Polling

How servers push data in real time.

• Polling: simple but wasteful
• SSE: easy one-way streaming over HTTP
• WebSocket: full two-way, real time
• Plan for connection state at scale

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #18: Load Balancers: L4 vs L7

What your load balancer can actually see.

• L4: fast, protocol-agnostic, connection-level
• L7: smart, HTTP-aware, request-level
• L7 enables canaries, path routing, TLS offload
• Many architectures use both

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #19: Load Balancing Algorithms

Which server gets the next request?.

• Round robin: the simple default
• Least connections: for uneven work
• Hashing: for stickiness and caches
• Power of two: cheap and surprisingly good

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #20: Reverse Proxy vs Forward Proxy

Same middleman, opposite sides.

• Forward proxy: speaks for clients
• Reverse proxy: speaks for servers
• Reverse proxies power LBs, CDNs, gateways
• Ask: who configured it, and who does it hide?

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #21: API Gateway

One front door for all your services.

• One front door for many services
• Centralizes auth, limits, routing
• Aggregates calls for chatty clients
• Keep it thin, and highly available

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #22: Content Delivery Networks

Putting your content next to your users.

• CDNs cache content near users
• Miss → fetch from origin; hit → fast
• Cache-Control headers set the rules
• Version static files, keep HTML short-lived

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #23: Service Discovery

How services find each other when IPs keep changing.

• Instances register; callers look up
• Heartbeats remove dead instances
• Client-side vs server-side discovery
• In Kubernetes: Services + DNS

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #24: Service Mesh

Networking superpowers without touching code.

• Sidecar proxies handle service traffic
• Control plane configures them all
• mTLS, retries, canaries, metrics for free
• Costs: latency, memory, complexity

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #25: SQL vs NoSQL

Choosing the right kind of database.

• SQL: structure, joins, transactions
• NoSQL: scale and flexibility
• Model NoSQL around your queries
• Many systems use both (polyglot persistence)

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #26: ACID vs BASE

Two philosophies of data correctness.

• ACID: correct, every time
• BASE: available, eventually correct
• WAL makes durability possible
• Match the model to the cost of being wrong

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #27: Database Indexing: B-Trees & LSM Trees

Why one index turns seconds into milliseconds.

• Indexes turn O(n) scans into O(log n) lookups
• B-trees: balanced, read- and range-friendly
• LSM trees: write-optimized, compaction
• Index what you query, nothing more

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #28: Normalization vs Denormalization

Store each fact once, or copy it for speed?.

• Normalize by default: correctness first
• Denormalize hot read paths deliberately
• Every copy is a consistency obligation
• Let the database maintain copies when it can

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #29: Database Replication

Keeping copies of your data in sync.

• Single-leader: simple, no write conflicts
• Multi-leader: local writes, needs conflict handling
• Leaderless: quorums, highly available
• Sync = safe but slow; async = fast but lossy

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #30: Sharding & Partitioning

Splitting data that no longer fits on one machine.

• Sharding scales data and writes horizontally
• The shard key is the most important decision
• Cross-shard queries are expensive
• Plan for resharding from day one

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #31: Consistent Hashing

Add or remove servers without reshuffling everything.

• Servers and keys share one hash ring
• Keys go to the next server clockwise
• Membership changes move ~1/N of keys
• Virtual nodes keep the spread even

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #32: Read Replicas & Read/Write Splitting

Scaling a read-heavy database.

• Writes to the primary, reads to replicas
• Scales reads almost linearly
• Replication lag → stale reads
• Write-heavy? Shard instead

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #33: Key-Value Stores

The simplest, fastest database model.

• Get/put by key: simple and fast
• Partition by hash to scale out
• No rich queries: design keys carefully
• Redis data structures go far beyond caching

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #34: Wide-Column Stores

Built for massive write throughput.

• Partition key → node; clustering key → order
• Masterless, replicated, write-optimized
• Design tables around queries
• Avoid unbounded partitions

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #35: Document Databases

Store data the way your app uses it.

• Documents match how apps read data
• Embed what you read together
• Reference what grows unbounded
• Index the fields you query

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #36: Graph Databases

When the relationships are the data.

• Nodes, relationships, properties
• Traversals follow pointers, not joins
• Shines on connected, deep queries
• Use other stores for bulk analytics

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #37: Time-Series Databases

Built for metrics, sensors and events over time.

• Append-heavy, time-ordered data
• Compression + downsampling + retention
• Fast range and aggregate queries
• Watch tag cardinality

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #38: Object Storage

Where the internet keeps its files.

• Flat namespace of keys, HTTP API
• Cheap, durable, nearly infinite
• Presigned URLs for direct upload/download
• Not for low-latency random writes

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #39: Distributed File Systems

One giant filesystem across thousands of disks.

• Files → big blocks → many machines
• Replicated 3× for durability
• Metadata server + data servers
• In the cloud, object storage mostly took over

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #40: Data Lake vs Warehouse vs Lakehouse

Where your analytics data should live.

• Warehouse: clean, structured, fast SQL
• Lake: raw, cheap, flexible
• Lakehouse: both, via open table formats
• Govern your lake or it becomes a swamp

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #41: Connection Pooling

Stop paying for a new handshake on every request.

• Reuse connections instead of reconnecting
• Small, well-sized pools beat huge ones
• Use a shared pooler for many clients
• Serverless functions especially need one

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #42: Transaction Isolation Levels

What concurrent transactions are allowed to see.

• Higher isolation = fewer anomalies, less concurrency
• Most DBs default to read committed
• Defaults don’t prevent lost updates
• Use atomic updates, locks or SERIALIZABLE

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #43: Caching Layers

Every place a response can be served faster.

• Cache at every layer, closest to the user first
• Hit ratio drives average latency
• Cache read-heavy, slow-changing data
• Freshness is the price you pay

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #44: Cache Write Strategies

Cache-aside, write-through, write-back, write-around.

• Cache-aside: the sensible default
• Write-through: fresh, slower writes
• Write-back: fast, risk of loss
• Write-around: don’t cache what isn’t re-read

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #45: Cache Eviction: LRU, LFU, TTL

Deciding what to throw out when memory is full.

• LRU: simple, recency-based default
• LFU: protects long-term favorites
• TTL: bounds staleness, not size
• Modern caches blend recency + frequency

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #46: Cache Invalidation

Keeping cached copies from going stale.

• TTL on everything
• Delete on write (cache-aside)
• CDC makes invalidation automatic
• Races exist: use leases or versions

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #47: Cache Stampede

When one expiring key takes down your database.

• Hot key expiry → herd of identical misses
• Single-flight / locks: one recompute
• Serve stale while refreshing
• Jitter TTLs; pre-warm before peaks

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #48: Distributed Caching

Scaling a cache beyond one machine.

• Shard keys across nodes by hash
• Replicate each shard for failover
• L1 local + L2 shared = fast and scalable
• Design keys for co-location

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #49: Hot Keys

When one key gets more traffic than a whole shard can take.

• Hashing can’t spread one key
• Reads: replicate the key + local caches
• Writes: shard the counter
• Detect hot keys before they melt a shard

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #50: Message Queues

Decouple services and absorb traffic spikes.

• Producers and consumers are decoupled
• Spikes become backlogs, not outages
• Scale workers to match the queue
• Design for retries and duplicates

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #51: Pub/Sub

Broadcast events to everyone who cares.

• One event → many independent reactions
• Publishers don’t know subscribers
• Topic + queue per service = durable fan-out
• Events are contracts: version them

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #52: Event Streaming with Kafka

The distributed log behind real-time data.

• A replayable, partitioned, replicated log
• Ordering per partition, parallelism across them
• Consumer groups read independently
• Use keys to keep related events ordered

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #53: Delivery Guarantees

At-most-once, at-least-once, exactly-once.

• At-most-once: may lose
• At-least-once: may duplicate
• “Exactly-once” = at-least-once + idempotency
• Default to at-least-once, make consumers idempotent

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #54: Idempotency

Making retries safe.

• Retries are inevitable: make them safe
• Idempotency keys for client requests
• Unique constraints and dedupe tables
• Prefer “set” over “increment”

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #55: Dead Letter Queues

Where poison messages go instead of blocking everything.

• Poison messages must not block the queue
• Max attempts → dead letter queue
• Alert, inspect, fix, redrive
• Retry transient errors, dead-letter permanent ones

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #56: Backpressure

What to do when work arrives faster than you can handle it.

• Mismatched rates must be handled explicitly
• Options: buffer, drop, slow down, scale
• Backpressure signals travel upstream
• Unbounded buffers are delayed crashes

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #57: Batch vs Stream Processing

Process data later in bulk, or the moment it arrives?.

• Batch: simple, efficient, delayed
• Stream: immediate, stateful, trickier
• Windows & watermarks tame unbounded data
• Many teams now default to streaming + replay

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #58: Consensus: Raft & Paxos

How machines agree when some of them fail.

• Consensus = agreement despite failures
• Raft: leader, log replication, elections
• Majority quorum: 2f + 1 nodes
• Use etcd/ZooKeeper; don’t write your own

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #59: Leader Election

Making sure exactly one node is in charge.

• Leases: hold leadership only while alive
• Use a consensus service, not homegrown code
• Assume a leader can pause and come back
• Fencing tokens make that safe

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #60: Two-Phase Commit

All-or-nothing across multiple databases.

• Prepare (vote) → commit or abort
• Gives atomicity across resources
• Blocking, slow, coordinator-dependent
• Microservices usually prefer sagas

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #61: The Saga Pattern

Long transactions as a chain of undoable steps.

• Local transactions + compensations
• Choreography or orchestration
• Eventual consistency, no isolation
• Idempotent steps, persisted state

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #62: Event Sourcing

Store what happened, derive what is.

• Events are the source of truth
• State is a fold over events
• Audit, time travel and new views for free
• Plan for schema evolution and snapshots

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #63: CQRS

Separate models for writing and reading.

• Commands and queries use different models
• Read models are optimized per use case
• Expect lag between write and read side
• Don’t use it for simple CRUD apps

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #64: Distributed Locks

Mutual exclusion across many machines.

• SET NX PX: acquire with expiry
• Token check on release
• Pauses and expiry break naive locks
• Fence writes with increasing tokens

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #65: Clocks: Logical & Vector

Ordering events when wall clocks can’t be trusted.

• Don’t order distributed events by wall clock alone
• Lamport clocks: cheap causal ordering
• Vector clocks: detect concurrent writes
• Spanner’s TrueTime waits out its uncertainty

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #66: Unique ID Generation

Billions of IDs, no collisions, no bottleneck.

• Avoid a central counter at scale
• Snowflake: time + machine + sequence
• UUIDv7: a time-sortable standard UUID
• Handle clock skew explicitly

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #67: Gossip Protocols

Spreading information like a rumor.

• Random peer-to-peer exchanges
• Reaches everyone in ~log N rounds
• Powers membership and failure detection
• Fast enough, not instant

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #68: Quorum Reads & Writes

Tuning consistency with R + W > N.

• R + W > N → reads see the latest write
• Tune W and R for speed vs safety
• Majority quorums tolerate minority failures
• Watch for sloppy quorums

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #69: Bloom Filters

“Definitely not” or “probably yes”, in a few bits.

• Bit array + k hash functions
• “No” is certain; “yes” is probable
• ~10 bits per item for 1% error
• Great as a cheap pre-check before expensive lookups

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #70: Merkle Trees

Find differences in huge datasets by comparing hashes.

• Hashes of hashes, up to one root
• Find differences in O(log n) steps
• Detect tampering and prove inclusion
• Behind repair, Git and blockchains

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #71: Rate Limiting Algorithms

Token bucket, leaky bucket and sliding windows, explained.

• Limits protect fairness, cost and uptime
• Token bucket: average rate + burst capacity
• Sliding window avoids edge spikes
• Enforce at the edge, store counters in Redis

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #72: Circuit Breakers

Stop calling a service that is already down.

• Closed → Open → Half-open → Closed
• Fail fast instead of waiting on timeouts
• Gives failing services room to recover
• Pair with fallbacks and alerts

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #73: Retries, Backoff & Jitter

How to retry without making an outage worse.

• Retry transient failures, not bad requests
• Back off exponentially, with a cap
• Add jitter to break up waves
• Retry only idempotent work, at one layer

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #74: Timeouts & Bulkheads

Contain failures so one slow dependency can’t sink the ship.

• Every remote call gets a timeout
• Base timeouts on measured latency
• Bulkheads isolate pools per dependency
• A slow service should never sink the ship

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #75: Graceful Degradation

Keep the core working when parts of the system fail.

• Separate critical from optional features
• Every optional dependency has a fallback
• Prefer stale or partial data over errors
• Test failure modes before users find them

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels

System Design #76: Health Checks & Heartbeats

How systems know which machines are alive.

• Health checks: someone asks; heartbeats: node tells
• Liveness restarts, readiness routes
• Deep checks can cause cascading outages
• Use thresholds to avoid false alarms

Take the quiz in the video, then save this for your next interview.

#systemdesign #softwareengineering #backend #codinginterview #distributedsystems #programming #techreels
